plan_title: EOG SPG Holdings, Inc. Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan for SPG CO2 Bowie Facility, Montague County, TX
ama_definition: The simulated separate-phase CO2 plume (3% saturation cutoff) at the end of the 12-year injection period in 2035 plus a half-mile buffer, which fully contains the year-2040 plume (p34-35).
mma_definition: The simulated stabilized plume (3% saturation cutoff, stable about year 2225) plus the required half-mile buffer (p33-34).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: No pathway is rated likely. The two project wellbores (the only penetrations of the injection zone) and the short surface piping between meter and wellhead are the pathways actually instrumented; faults/fractures are rated low (fault slip potential <10%) and the 2,200-ft confining system extremely unlikely to leak; other existing wells are >1,400 ft above the injection zone (p35-44).
baseline_summary: Mixed: operational baselines from continuous surface and downhole pressure/temperature data (to be established by July 17, 2023), plus pre-injection baseline surveys: initial MIT, initial pressure transient analysis from injection tests, and pre-injection saturation and mechanical integrity logs in both project wells (p46-47).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with mass balance (RR-4, RR-10, RR-12); any leak mass noted in the annual report; records kept at least three years (p40, p47-50). The attached Class II permit also requires annual H-10 reporting, annual annulus test (H-5) and a fluid migration/pressure monitoring report to TXRRC (p54-55). No commitment to publish measurement data.

rows.detail: High-pressure Coriolis mass meter (FW46045INJ, ±0.15%) downstream of the injection compressor, less than 210 ft from the wellhead; composition from gas chromatograph upstream of compressor, validated by quarterly gas samples; NIST-traceable calibration.
rows.location: Injection facility, between final compressor and Hinkle Trust #1 wellhead
rows.evidence_quote: The high pressure coriolis mass meter used in the system has an accuracy of ±0.15%

rows.detail: Continuous wellhead pressure monitoring and continuous downhole pressure/temperature from gauges on tubing and casing, fed to a real-time data acquisition system with alarms and operational set points; data archived and trended.
rows.location: Hinkle Trust #1 wellhead and downhole; Billy Henderson #5
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviation from operational baseline trends investigated as possible leak signal; set points keep downhole pressure below fault-slip thresholds.
rows.evidence_quote: will be continuously monitored via the project's real-time data acquisition system

rows.detail: Surface pressures on all casing strings and downhole gauges on the intermediate casing collected continuously in both wells to watch the long-string annular space; permit requires at least weekly tubing-casing annulus monitoring.
rows.location: Hinkle Trust #1 and Billy Henderson #5, all casing strings
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviations from operational baselines investigated; wellbore leak leads to volume estimate and corrective action.
rows.evidence_quote: surface pressures on all strings of casing is collected continuously in both wells

rows.detail: Annual MIT on Hinkle Trust #1 as required by the Class II permit (annual annulus pressure test, Form H-5); initial MIT at completion serves as baseline for later tests.
rows.trigger_or_response: Results compared to initial MIT and TXRRC standards; additional MIT and corrosion logging if a wellbore leak is suspected.
rows.evidence_quote: an annual mechanical integrity test (MIT) will be conducted in the injection well as prescribed in the Class II

rows.detail: Downhole pressure-temperature gauges and fiber across the injection zone in the Billy Henderson #5 monitor well (1,600 ft from injector) and in the injector, read continuously; yearly pressure transient analysis; permit requires wireline BHP test every five years.
rows.location: Billy Henderson #5 monitor well and Hinkle Trust #1, middle Ellenburger
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexplained pressure change: sensor validation, extended pressure transient analysis, additional saturation logging; reservoir simulation to quantify.
rows.evidence_quote: pressure-temperature gauges and fiber monitoring instrumentation were installed across the injection zone

rows.detail: Field personnel conduct auditory, visual and olfactory (AVO) inspections of the injection site and surface equipment; Table 8 lists weekly, text says daily to weekly, before, during and after injection.
rows.location: Injection site, flowmeter to injection wellhead
rows.trigger_or_response: Signs of CO2 leakage: corrective action; verification by AVO, FLIR camera and enhanced gas monitoring; quantify from process conditions.
rows.evidence_quote: Field personnel will conduct daily to weekly inspections at the injection site pre-, during, and post-injection.

rows.detail: Personnel wear personal H2S monitors (OSHA-calibrated, 0.5 ppm sensitivity, 10 ppm low alarm) during inspections; H2S used as a proxy for CO2 since the stream contains both.
rows.location: Worn by field personnel at the injection site
rows.trigger_or_response: H2S indication treated as CO2 presence; investigate and correct.
rows.evidence_quote: Personnel will wear personal H2S monitors calibrated to OSHA standards with a detection sensitivity of 0.5 ppm

rows.detail: FLIR (optical gas imaging) camera inspection and unspecified 'enhanced gas monitoring' of surface facilities, only as verification steps after a suspected leak.
rows.location: Surface facilities at the injection site
rows.trigger_or_response: Suspected surface facility leak: FLIR inspection and enhanced gas monitoring to confirm or rule out.

rows.detail: Pressure-temperature gauges and fiber installed above the injection zone in the Billy Henderson #5 monitor and on the Hinkle Trust #1 intermediate casing; continuous data; listed as confining system detection. Depth relative to top of confining zone not stated.
rows.location: Both project wells, above the middle Ellenburger
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomalous pressure/temperature: validate sensors, deploy wireline sensors, saturation logging, extended pressure transient analysis.
rows.evidence_quote: above the injection zone (gauges and fiber) to allow for monitoring of pressure and temperature responses across the wellbore

rows.detail: Yearly time-lapse saturation surveys and yearly corrosion/mechanical integrity logging in the two project wells, compared to pre-injection baseline saturation and integrity logs; additional saturation logs if a leak is suspected. Also permanent DTS/DAS fiber on well casing, recording continuously.
rows.trigger_or_response: Saturation change outside injection zone: additional logging, sensor checks; saturation change used to estimate leaked mass.
rows.evidence_quote: Initial pre-injection surveys have been conducted for both saturation and mechanical integrity and will serve to establish baselines

rows.detail: One-time review of the USGS earthquake catalog showing one earthquake in Montague County in 100 years; no seismometers and no commitment to ongoing seismic monitoring.
rows.evidence_quote: Only one earthquake in Montague County has been recorded in the last 100 years

rows.detail: In-house 3D seismic used only for characterization and fault mapping; 'additional geophysical imaging surveys' are something SPG 'will consider' to help quantify a verified leak.
rows.evidence_quote: SPG will also consider conducting additional appropriate geophysical imaging surveys

rows.detail: Yearly pressure transient analysis of injection and fall-off data from both wells to check consistency of injection and confining zone behavior against the initial test-based baseline.
rows.trigger_or_response: Change in transient behavior: extended analysis, additional logging; reservoir model used to back out leaked mass.
rows.evidence_quote: Subsequent pressure transient analyses are in progress and will continue to be performed when operationally feasible

rows.detail: Review of TXRRC permitting activity across the project area each quarter to catch new wells that could create a leakage risk in the MMA.
rows.trigger_or_response: Proposed well posing risk: take action; if drilled, update MRV plan and add monitoring near the new well.
rows.evidence_quote: SPG intends to monitor permitting activity across the entire project area on a quarterly basis

rows.detail: Subpart W calculation methods for fugitive equipment leaks between the injection meter and wellhead; venting occurs upstream of the meter so is not subtracted.
rows.location: Surface equipment between flow meter and wellhead
rows.evidence_quote: the methods outlined in 40 CFR §98 subpart W will be used to quantify those amounts

rows.detail: Reservoir simulation history-matched to observed pressure or saturation anomalies to estimate leaked CO2 mass through faults, wellbores or the confining system; enhanced surveillance (saturation surveys) on nearby EOG-operated wells; possible new monitoring wells.
rows.trigger_or_response: Verified leak: simulate leakage cases to match data and report mass in annual report.
rows.evidence_quote: reservoir simulation will likely be an essential tool to quantify the magnitude of the leak in those cases

rows.detail: Class II permit condition (Appendix A): static bottomhole pressure test before injection and wireline BHP test at least every five years; fluid migration and pressure monitoring report filed with each MIT.
rows.trigger_or_response: Fluid found outside permitted interval: permit suspended and injection stopped until migration eliminated.
rows.evidence_quote: Operator shall conduct a BHP test at least once every five (5) years

notes: No production occurs (p48), so production_monitoring is coded not_found. Table 8 lists both visual inspection and personal H2S monitors as 'Weekly' while Section 3.7 says 'daily to weekly' inspections; weekly used. The above-zone gauges are described only as 'above the injection zone'; the plan does not say whether they sit above the top of the upper confining system, so the above_zone_monitoring row may overstate coverage. 'Enhanced gas monitoring' (Table 9) is undefined and was folded into fixed_gas_detectors as a conditional verification step rather than atmospheric_co2. Additional geophysical imaging surveys appear in Table 10 as a quantification method but the text says SPG 'will consider' them, so active_seismic is coded mentioned_only rather than conditional. The last 'other' row comes from the TXRRC permit reproduced in Appendix A (p53-56), not the MRV narrative. Pages 10, 12, 13, 32, 33, 35 are essentially figure-only but no needed section is missing; appendix B is a generic drilling permit. Permanent DTS/DAS fiber is coded under cased_hole_logging, as in v1.3.
